title: Prioritized catalog gating with customer-weighted intake paths and shadow canary
creator: Asha Patel
description: Context: Enterprise customers increasingly request specific model variants, short-term pins, and slow deprecations tied to regulatory review. Our current intake and triage flows overload the PM queue and lack a deterministic way to balance customer urgency, compatibility risk, and platform capacity. This ticket proposes a new intake gating flow for the model catalog that combines: (1) a customer-weighted priority score, (2) a compatibility "lattice" to match customer workloads to model variants, and (3) a shadow-canary on onboarding to detect regressions without affecting existing tenants. Goal: reduce manual triage time by ~40%, ensure high-impact customer requests reach canary staging in 2 sprints, and prevent silent quality regressions during fast onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic priority score is defined and automated in the intake form; unit tests for scoring exist
An intake UI change routes requests into 3 lanes (fast-path, standard evaluation, research review) based on score
Compatibility lattice mapping exists for top 15 enterprise customers (data type, token profile, latency SLOs) and can be expanded
Shadow-canary orchestration deploys new model variants for 2% of customer traffic in read-only / eval mode for 48-72 hours
Dashboards show time-to-canary, percent of requests auto-routed, and false-positive/negative rate for auto-routing
Rollout plan with rollback and deprecation cooling period documented and signed off by Legal and Security
proposed_solution: Add a customer-weighted scoring layer to the model intake form that combines explicit customer signals (SLA tier, active contracts, number of users) and implicit signals (recent 30d traffic, feature parity requirements). Use the score to auto-route requests into: Fast-Path (customer-weighted score >= 80), Standard Eval (40-79), and Research/Low (<=39). Implement a compatibility lattice (CSV-driven) that matches request metadata to recommended model variants and quantization levels. For Fast-Path items, create a shadow-canary step: deploy the requested variant into a read-only evaluation pool wired to the requesting customer's telemetry for 48-72 hours; surface regressions and automatic rollback suggestions. Integrate results into an automated PRD generation template for final review. Ensure RBAC and auditing hooks exist for enterprise-only pins and deprecations.
scoring_formula: score = round(min(100, (0.4*SLA_tier_score) + (0.25*contract_value_norm) + (0.15*30d_traffic_norm) + (0.1*security_sensitivity) + (0.1*customer_risk_flag) ))\nWhere SLA_tier_score in {100,70,40} for enterprise/dedicated/self-serve, contract_value_norm is percentile-normalized, 30d_traffic_norm is percentile-normalized, security_sensitivity is 0-10, customer_risk_flag is binary*20. The weights are tunable via admin UI.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Spec review with Eng (runtime, infra) and Legal; finalize scoring weights and lattice attributes
Week 2: Intake form API + front-end changes; compatibility lattice CSV spec and admin upload UI
Week 3: Shadow-canary infra (eval-only routing, telemetry hooks) implementation by ENG; integrate with Console dashboards
Week 4: Internal pilot with 3 enterprise customers and 5 sandbox tenants; collect regression signals and iterate
Week 5: Expand to top 15 customers, update docs, finalize runbook and deprecation cooling period
Week 6: GA rollout behind feature flag; monitor metrics for 4 weeks before full removal of manual gating
metrics: Median time from intake -> canary start (target <= 14 days for Fast-Path)
Regression detection rate in shadow-canary and time-to-detect (target detect within 48 hours)
